<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
          <jats:p>
            The microbial community structure and spatial distribution of microorganisms and their in situ activities in anaerobic granules were investigated by 16S rRNA gene-based molecular techniques and microsensors for CH
            <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
            , H
            <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
            , pH, and the oxidation-reduction potential (ORP). The 16S rRNA gene-cloning analysis revealed that the clones related to the phyla
            <jats:italic>Alphaproteobacteria</jats:italic>
            (detection frequency, 51%),
            <jats:italic>Firmicutes</jats:italic>
            (20%),
            <jats:italic>Chloroflexi</jats:italic>
            (9%), and
            <jats:italic>Betaproteobacteria</jats:italic>
            (8%) dominated the bacterial clone library, and the predominant clones in the archaeal clone library were affiliated with
            <jats:italic>Methanosaeta</jats:italic>
            (73%). In situ hybridization with oligonucleotide probes at the phylum level revealed that these microorganisms were numerically abundant in the granule. A layered structure of microorganisms was found in the granule, where
            <jats:italic>Chloroflexi</jats:italic>
            and
            <jats:italic>Betaproteobacteria</jats:italic>
            were present in the outer shell of the granule,
            <jats:italic>Firmicutes</jats:italic>
            were found in the middle layer, and aceticlastic
            <jats:italic>Archaea</jats:italic>
            were restricted to the inner layer. Microsensor measurements for CH
            <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
            , H
            <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
            , pH, and ORP revealed that acid and H
            <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
            production occurred in the upper part of the granule, below which H
            <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
            consumption and CH
            <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
            production were detected. Direct comparison of the in situ activity distribution with the spatial distribution of the microorganisms implied that
            <jats:italic>Chloroflexi</jats:italic>
            contributed to the degradation of complex organic compounds in the outermost layer, H
            <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
            was produced mainly by
            <jats:italic>Firmicutes</jats:italic>
            in the middle layer, and
            <jats:italic>Methanosaeta</jats:italic>
            produced CH
            <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
            in the inner layer. We determined the effective diffusion coefficient for H
            <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
            in the anaerobic granules to be 2.66 × 10
            <jats:sup>−5</jats:sup>
            cm
            <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
            s
            <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
            , which was 57% in water.
          </jats:p>
title: Layered Structure of Bacterial and Archaeal Communities and Their In Situ Activities in Anaerobic Granules
